title: First-Principles Claim Ladder Game — Gemini model variant
description: A developer-operated Gemini rerun of the canonical First-Principles Claim Ladder Game brief, preserved as an auditable PathForge Labs model variant rather than a community fork.

comparison_basis.opening_prompt_exact: Can you build a self-contained one-file HTML game called First-Principles Claim Ladder where I test a big plan by moving claim, assumption, evidence, and experiment cards up a ladder, score whether the plan holds or collapses, and copy or download a reasoning receipt I can keep offline?
acceptance_criteria: Provide distinct claim, assumption, evidence, and experiment cards in one understandable ladder workflow.
Let the user move or classify cards and run a visible holds-versus-collapses reasoning check.
Produce a meaningful reasoning score or assessment tied to the current ladder state.
Provide a copyable or downloadable reasoning receipt that includes the experiment or next test.
Produce one complete self-contained HTML file that is immediately usable in a browser.
Operate offline with no external APIs, hosted generation, CDNs, remote fonts, scripts, stylesheets, or fragile dependencies.
Avoid unsafe HTML sinks, eval-like execution, inline event handlers, modal dialogs, and deprecated clipboard handling.
Avoid page-level horizontal overflow at 390 by 844 and at desktop width.
Keep essential controls visible, keyboard or touch reachable, and truthful about their current state.
Preserve exact prompt, response, source, and artifact-version evidence for the run.
comparison_basis.adaptive_repair_policy: Preserve and score the first real artifact. Continue only when verification proves a concrete defect or a source-capture failure; use the same source session and model; name the observed defect in ordinary language; preserve every real artifact version; stop as soon as the artifact passes; prefer no more than three total prompts and go beyond three only for a documented concrete lane reason such as a verification-proven regression, truncation, or mechanical capture failure.
comparison_basis.independence_note: Gemini received the invariant brief in a fresh session and was not shown the historical implementation, screenshots, source code, or another provider's output.

agent_notes: Model settings: Gemini web; Pro mode.
PathForge Labs provenance: developer-operated comparison run; not a user, community fork, vote, bookmark, or engagement event.
Prompt count: 3. The first repair removed inline handlers, unsafe HTML rendering, and an alert dialog; the second verification-driven repair reflowed the cramped 390px add-card form.
All three real artifact versions are preserved under public/artifacts. The third artifact is the default selectable version for this model run.

Final verification passed all ten fixed contract checks, static safety, JavaScript parsing, all four card types, drag/drop, both collapse and holds outcomes, exact receipt copy and download, desktop rendering, and measured 390x844 no-overflow checks.

verification_notes: The final artifact's single inline script parsed successfully.

Static scan found no external URL, remote dependency, fetch, XHR, unsafe HTML sink, eval-like execution, inline handler, document.write, modal API, deprecated clipboard handling, or negative letter spacing.

Direct verification created Claim, Assumption, Evidence, and Experiment cards; moved them through the visible ladder; observed both LADDER COLLAPSES and LADDER HOLDS feedback; and produced a 380-character reasoning receipt containing every card type and the validated result.
Receipt copy was byte-identical and download produced reasoning-receipt.txt with byte-identical text.
Fresh 390x844 and 1440x1000 measurements reported zero horizontal overflow and zero console errors; at 390px the form, input, selector, and Add Card button each measured 310px wide.

steps.title: Build the invariant Claim Ladder brief
steps.prompt_exact: Can you build a self-contained one-file HTML game called First-Principles Claim Ladder where I test a big plan by moving claim, assumption, evidence, and experiment cards up a ladder, score whether the plan holds or collapses, and copy or download a reasoning receipt I can keep offline?
steps.response_summary: Gemini produced the first complete one-file Claim Ladder game.
steps.notes: Preserved first artifact. Static verification found inline handlers, innerHTML sinks, and an alert dialog.

steps.title: Repair unsafe event and rendering patterns
steps.prompt_exact: I tested the saved file and my public viewer rejects three concrete implementation choices: the drag/drop and buttons use inline event attributes, the cards and result banner are built with innerHTML, and copying opens an alert dialog. Replace those with addEventListener wiring, createElement/textContent rendering, and an inline copy-status message while preserving the ladder game, scoring, receipt copy/download, and complete offline HTML.
steps.response_summary: Gemini returned a complete safe-listener and textContent-rendered Claim Ladder.
steps.continuation_reason: Verification-proven defects: inline event attributes, innerHTML rendering, and alert() violated public mount gates.

steps.title: Reflow the true-mobile add-card form
steps.prompt_exact: On a real 390 by 844 phone viewport, the add-card form stays in two columns and squeezes the type selector and card text field to about 83 pixels each, clipping their labels and placeholders. Reflow that form to one full-width column on narrow screens with readable controls and a full-width Add Card button. Keep every existing safety repair plus the ladder, scoring, receipt copy and download behavior unchanged, and return the complete self-contained HTML again.
